title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices. It covers severity definitions, the incident lifecycle (detection through postmortem), runbook standards, rotation and escalation policies, game day guidance, and templates for status page and customer communications. The goal is predictable, blameless, fast response that preserves customer trust and minimizes customer impact.

Scope:
- Applies to all production services that serve customer traffic (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private control plane, serving runtime, telemetry).
- Includes engineering (SRE/infra/serving-runtime), product incident owners, and customer-facing teams (support, success).

Goals / Principles:
- Safety: protect customer data and availability first.
- Speed: detect and reduce time-to-mitigation and time-to-recovery (TTM / TTR).
- Observability-driven: prefer actions with measurable signals.
- Blameless postmortems: focus on systemic fixes and learning.

1) Incident severity matrix
- Sev 0 (SEV0) — Critical outage: major global outage or data loss, almost all customers affected, immediate executive notification. Target TTR: 1 hour.
- Sev 1 (SEV1) — Major degradation: significant latency/errors for many customers or large-paying customer impact. Target TTR: 4 hours.
- Sev 2 (SEV2) — Partial impairment: subset of customers impacted, degraded feature; Target TTR: 24 hours.
- Sev 3 (SEV3) — Minor/operational: limited impact or single-customer non-critical bug; Target TTR: next business day.

2) Roles and responsibilities
- Primary on-call (Primary): First responder. Owns triage, mitigation, and documentation until handoff.
- Secondary on-call (Secondary): Backup and escalation target for Primary.
- Incident Commander (IC): For SEV0/SEV1, designated IC coordinates cross-team response, decisions, and external comms.
- Communications Lead: Drafts status updates and coordinates customer-facing messages.
- Postmortem lead: Authors the blameless postmortem and tracks action items.
- Support liaison: Routes customer tickets and captures customer impact details.

3) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts should include service, cluster, region, recent deploys, error rates, and runbook link.
   - Primary acknowledges within 5 minutes for SEV0/SEV1; 30 minutes for SEV2/SEV3.

2. Triage
   - Primary determines scope: affected services, customers, and any correlation with deploys or infra events.
   - Set incident severity. If severity escalates to SEV0/SEV1, declare an incident channel (Slack + incident doc) and appoint IC.

3. Mitigation & Containment
   - Follow runbooks for immediate mitigation (traffic shift, autoscaling fixes, revert deploy, restart service).
   - Document commands run, timestamps, and who performed each action in the incident doc.

4. Recovery & Verification
   - Verify mitigation by checking SLO-related signals (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, success rate, queue lengths).
   - Confirm with affected customers via Support if necessary.

5. Communication
   - Update Status Page at each major incident milestone (Investigating -> Identified -> Mitigating -> Service degraded/outage -> Resolved).
   - Use the comms templates below for status page and customer emails.

6. Post-incident work
   - Create a blameless postmortem within 72 hours. Include timeline, root cause analysis, action items with owners and due dates, and verification plan.

4) Runbook standards and templates
- All runbooks must follow the canonical template and be stored in confluence under the service folder. Runbooks are executable playbooks — include commands, dashboards, and quick rollback steps.

Runbook template (plain text):
- Service: <service-name>
- Owner: <team/name>
- Pager: <pager-id>
- Symptoms / Alerts: (list of alerts that map to this runbook)
- Initial triage checklist: (e.g., check pods, check ingress, check last deploy)
- Short mitigation steps (ordered, idempotent where possible)
- Rollback steps (if mitigation involves a deploy)
- Verification steps & dashboards to watch
- Post-incident notes link

Example: api-gateway-runbook (summary)
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate on api-gateway (alert api-gateway-5xx-high)
- Initial triage: 1) Check control-plane for config changes, 2) tail gateway logs for 502/503 origin errors, 3) check upstream serving-runtime p95 latency
- Mitigation: 1) Route traffic to fallback pool (cli: ri route set --pool fallback), 2) scale up gateway replicas, 3) temporarily disable new routing rules
- Verification: 5xx rate < 1% for 10 minutes and p95 latency within SLO

5) On-call rotations and handoffs
- Rotation length: default 1 week (Mon 00:00 UTC — Sun 23:59 UTC). Teams may run 2-week rotations with manager approval.
- Primary/Secondary pair: schedule two people per week (Primary + Secondary).
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack + calendar event):
  1) Summary of ongoing incidents / mitigations and pager status
  2) Any unfinished action items or postmortem drafts
  3) Known noisy alerts and recent flaps
  4) Local contact hours and planned unavailability
- Escalation policy:
  - Primary -> wait 10 minutes -> alert Secondary.
  - If no ack in 15 minutes or incident qualifies as SEV0, page oncall-leads and Engineering Director.

6) Game days (quarterly recommended)
- Objectives:
  - Validate runbooks end-to-end, exercise cross-team coordination, and stress-test monitoring and status page workflows.
- Planning checklist:
  1) Choose 2-3 realistic scenarios that map to common failure modes (e.g., GPU OOM causing serving-runtime degradation, control-plane DB failover, mass deploy causing broken model artifacts).
  2) Predefine hypotheses, monitoring targets, and customer impact levels.
  3) Schedule observers (SRE, product, support) and a debrief facilitator.
- Example agenda (half-day):
  - 15m: kickoff & goals
  - 60m: simulated incident 1 (detection through mitigation)
  - 30m: break & internal sync
  - 60m: simulated incident 2
  - 45m: retrospective & action item capture

7) Postmortem process and template
- Timeline: Postmortem created within 72 hours; final sign-off within two weeks.
- Tone: Blameless, timeline-driven, with clear RCA and measurable corrective actions.
- Minimum postmortem sections (plain text):
  - Title, Severity, Date/time, Authors, Summary (1-2 paragraphs), Timeline (minute-resolution for critical incidents), Root cause(s), Contributing factors, Corrective actions (owner + due date), Verification plan, Lessons learned, Related tickets/runbooks.

8) Status page and customer communications templates
- Status page states: investigating, identified, mitigating, degraded, partial_outage, major_outage, resolved.
- Status page update cadence: initial update within 15 minutes of SEV0/SEV1 declaration; subsequent updates every 30-60 minutes until resolved, then a final update with link to postmortem when available.

Status page template (short):
- Title: [Identified] Increased 5xx errors for Redwood API - [region]
- Body: We are investigating elevated 5xx responses for the Redwood API in <region>. Impact: ~X% of requests. Mitigation: Routing to fallback pool and scaling gateway. Next update: in 30 minutes.

Customer email template (for high-impact incidents):
- Subject: Incident update: Redwood API degraded in <region> — <short status>
- Body: Hello <Customer name>,
We are experiencing degraded service in <region> affecting API requests. Our engineering team has identified the root cause as <root-cause-summary>. We have applied mitigation to reduce impact and are monitoring. We will send updates every 30-60 minutes.
Regards,
Redwood Support

9) Tools, dashboards, and links (one-line list)
- Alerting: PagerDuty (service: ri-production), Slack (#incidents), Opsgenie for backups
- Dashboards: Grafana — API Latency (p50/p95/p99), Error rates, Serving-runtime Token throughput, GPU utilization
- On-call calendar & rota: Google Calendar (oncall@redwood.com)
- Incident docs: Confluence incident templates folder (link to runbook index)

10) Ownership, SLOs & measurable targets
- SLO examples (hosted API): availability 99.9% monthly, p95 latency < 600ms for short text generations, embedding success rate > 99.5%
- On-call KPI: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target: SEV0/SEV1 < 5 minutes; mean time to mitigate (MTTM) tracked per severity.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for the Primary on-call
- Acknowledge pager in PagerDuty & post in #incidents channel
- Create incident doc from template and pin in channel
- Run appropriate runbook and document steps
- Update status page and customer comms as required
- Handoff at rotation boundary with completed checklist

Appendix B — Example postmortem summary (short)
- Summary: On 2026-01-12, a configuration change caused routing rules to send 40% of traffic to a misconfigured pool, causing 502 errors. Mitigation involved reverting the change and rolling traffic to the previous pool.
- Actions: 1) Add deploy-time validation for routing rules (owner: infra-team, due: 2026-03-01), 2) Add automated rollback on surge of 5xx (owner: serving-runtime, due: 2026-02-15).
